en: him who is born for us,
and of a vir-, vir-, vir-,
and brought forth from a virgin's womb.
He is born into the world,
he is wrapped in swaddling cloths,
he is laid in a manger
the prince of hell has lost his spoils.
offering him gold, incense and myrrh.
you have come to the world,
I pour out praises to you.
therefore glory to God in the highest.
notes: Lines 6 and 7 of each stanza repeat a syllable of the word that opens line 8 (vir, vir of virgineo; dit, dit of perdidit; thus; o of ideo), as the tune asks; the translation repeats a word or syllable in the same places.
Line 1.2: voces puerulae, literally 'boyish voices', the voices of the choirboys.
Line 1.4: the Latin has no 'him': 'praising [the one] who is born for us'.
Line 4.1: clericuli, 'little clerics': the young clerks of a cathedral or school choir.
